However, existing methods still face challenges in complementary feature integration and coordinated optimization of feature selection and classifier parameters. To address the limited feature representation capability of handcrafted methods and the limited interpretability of deep learning approaches, this paper proposes a hybrid EEG artifact classification framework that integrates complementary feature representation with the joint optimization of feature selector and classifier parameters. Specifically, handcrafted temporal-spectral-entropy features are fused with deep features extracted by a lightweight ResNet-LSTM network. A novel Class Neighborhood Discrimination (CND) method is employed for discriminative feature selection, while an Adaptive Seagull Optimization Algorithm (ASOA) jointly optimizes the parameters of the CND feature selector and the Random Forest (RF) classifier within a unified optimization framework. Experimental results on the Temple University Artifact Corpus (TUAR) and clinical EEG recordings show that the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 99.30% on the originally constructed dataset and maintains 98.15% accuracy on an additional recording-independent clinical test set. The proposed method also shows consistent performance across multiple evaluation metrics, including MCC, Kappa, and GDR, and outperforms representative feature selection methods, optimization strategies, and classifiers. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively combines interpretability, discriminative feature representation, and joint optimization, providing an accurate and robust solution for epileptic EEG artifact classification.

papers.title: REV-ERBα deficiency exacerbates IL-33-mediated airway inflammation and airway hyperresponsiveness in mice.
papers.abstract: Asthma involves type 2 airway inflammation driven by epithelial-derived interleukin-33 (IL-33), a key mediator of allergic responses. REV-ERBα, a circadian transcriptional repressor, modulates pulmonary inflammation, but its role in IL-33-induced airway pathology remains unclear. Here we investigated IL-33-mediated pulmonary inflammation in wild-type and global Rev-erbα knockout mice exposed intranasally to recombinant IL-33. Loss of REV-ERBα markedly increased recruitment of eosinophils, neutrophils, innate lymphoid cells, and Th2 lymphocytes, exacerbated airway hyperresponsiveness, and elevated chemokines linked to type 2 inflammation. REV-ERBα deficiency also altered circadian clock protein expression, enhanced IL-33/ST2 signaling, and reduced epithelial barrier-associated proteins. These findings indicate that REV-ERBα restrains IL-33-driven airway inflammation and hyperresponsiveness, suggesting circadian mechanisms influence asthma pathogenesis and highlighting REV-ERBα as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Language prediction in multimodal contexts: The contribution of iconic gestures to anticipatory sentence comprehension.
papers.abstract: Evidence shows listeners predict upcoming words, and iconic gestures in face-to-face dialogue often precede their spoken referents. A recent framework proposes that early-onset gestures can pre-activate the meaning of upcoming nouns. This pre-registered EEG study tested this proposal. 81 Dutch adults watched videos of an actress producing discourses ending with a target noun. The noun was either predictable or not from the discourse. Each noun was paired with an iconic gesture whose stroke began either 520 msec (earlier) or 130 msec (later) before the noun. Discourse predictability produced the hypothesized post-target N400 reduction for predictable versus non-predictable items (H1). In the pre-target window, earlier gestures in non-predictable discourses elicited more negative amplitudes than in predictable discourses (H2a), suggesting that earlier gestures modulated neural responses when predictability was low. No comparable interaction was found for the opposite contrast (early-predictable vs late-predictable & late-non-predictable; H2c). In the post-target window, earlier gestures yielded a modest N400-like positivity relative to late gestures (H2e), but the interaction between gesture timing and discourse predictability (H2f) was not supported. A follow-up indicated that, in non-predictable discourses, later gestures produced a larger N400 than earlier gestures. Thus, the data confirm H1 and support H2a (and partially H2e), while H2c and H2f were not supported, suggesting that when speakers produce monologic discourses, earlier iconic gestures can aid anticipatory processing when linguistic predictions are weak, but their effect is limited and context-dependent. Together with the exploratory follow-up, the findings highlight a nuanced role of the influence of gesture timing on comprehension.
papers.journal: Cortex; a journal devoted to the study of the nervous system and behavior

papers.title: Research note: approach rather than avoidance: behavioral responses of broiler chicks repeatedly exposed to an autonomous mobile robot.
papers.abstract: Previous experience shapes animal behavior, and repeated exposure to non-aversive stimuli can reduce responses to subsequent challenges. Autonomous robots that navigate commercial broiler houses are being developed for environmental monitoring and have been shown to increase bird locomotion during their passage. However, whether this increased activity primarily reflects displacement or fear-induced avoidance, and how robot exposure influences behavioral responses, remains unclear. We assessed behavioral responses of broilers repeatedly exposed to the AviSense robot (Appelie Robotics) compared with non-exposed controls. From day 1 post-hatch, chicks were reared under commercial conditions in three 7.5 × 4.5 m pens containing approximately 500 birds each: one robot-exposed (RE) and two unexposed controls (CON). RE birds were exposed hourly to the robot for 10 min, whereas CON birds remained unexposed to it. At 13-15 d, chicks underwent individual behavioral tests; responses were analyzed with mixed-effects models. In a two-choice runway containing the robot and an unfamiliar basketball at opposite ends, RE chicks left the neutral zone sooner (P = 0.013) than controls. Treatment × Zone interaction P-values were 0.060 for latency to enter the stimulus close zones and 0.043 for time spent in these close zones. Fisher's LSD post hoc comparisons showed that RE chicks entered the robot close zone sooner than CON chicks (P = 0.004), spent more time in that zone than CON chicks (P = 0.004), and spent more time in the robot than the ball close zone (P = 0.036). In tests conducted without the robot, RE chicks showed shorter latency to ambulate in an open field (P = 0.002) and required more attempts to induce tonic immobility (P = 0.012), whereas social-reinstatement behavior was similar between treatments. Overall, previous robot exposure was associated with a robot-specific increase in subsequent proximity and with lower behavioral inhibition in independent fear-related contexts, providing no evidence that such exposure induced fear-driven avoidance. Repeated exposure to a robot may therefore promote familiarization and facilitate its integration into the birds' environment.

papers.title: Beyond total sleep time: Associations between sleep characteristics, weight status, and lifestyle behaviors in 6-10-year-old children.
papers.abstract: Sleep is increasingly recognized as a multifaceted construct; however, most studies rely on self-reported sleep duration and overlook other key characteristics. We analyzed cross-sectional data from the REACT project, which included 738 Portuguese children (398 girls) aged 6 to 10 years, using 7-day wrist actigraphy. Latent profile analysis based on total sleep time, sleep onset, wake-up, sleep efficiency, and sleep regularity identified four profiles: "Relatively Favorable Sleepers" (45.4%), "Late Starters & Short Sleepers" (34.3%), "Long Sleepers & Late Risers" (15.6%), and "Early Risers & Poor Quality" (4.7%). Children in the "Early Risers & Poor Quality" profile had higher odds of having overweight or obesity (OR: 2.09, 95% CI: 1.03-4.22) compared to those in the "Relatively Favorable Sleepers" profile. Children in the "Long Sleepers & Late Risers" profile were more likely to meet moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) recommendations (OR: 1.78, 95% CI: 1.05-3.03) and accumulated less sedentary time (β = -0.26, 95% CI: -0.50 to - 0.03). Conversely, the "Late Starters & Short Sleepers" profile was associated with higher sedentary time (β = 0.55, 95% CI: 0.38-0.73) and higher unhealthy diet scores (β = 0.41, 95% CI: 0.24-0.57), although no differences were observed in healthy diet scores. These findings highlight the value of multidimensional sleep assessment using objective measures for identifying pediatric subgroups at risk of adverse health outcomes.

papers.title: Race-ethnic minoritized veterans diagnosed with sleep apnea, insomnia, and COMISA at the Veterans Health Administration have lower all-cause mortality than Non-Hispanic White veterans.
papers.abstract: Few data exist exploring the relationship between sleep apnea (SA), insomnia, comorbid insomnia and sleep apnea (COMISA) and mortality among race-ethnic minoritized (REM) US veterans. This study compares all-cause mortality among Veterans Health Administration (VHA) patients diagnosed with these sleep disorders by race-ethnicity. The study included veterans with confirmed diagnoses and prescribed treatment for insomnia and/or SA, within the VHA, from 1999 to 2023. Using self-reported data, eight race-ethnicity groups were generated (i.e., Non-Hispanic White [NH-W], Non-Hispanic Black [NH-B], Hispanic White [H-W], Hispanic Black [H-B], Non-Hispanic Asian [NH-A], Non-Hispanic American Indian/Alaska Native [NH-AIAN], Non-Hispanic Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander [NH-NHPI]). Sleep diagnoses required International Classification of Diseases documentation. Additionally, insomnia was defined in those prescribed sleep medication or CBT-I while SA was defined in those prescribed positive airway pressure (PAP). All-cause mortality was extracted from national databases. For each sleep disorder, multivariable logistic regression determined the association between race-ethnicity and all-cause mortality, using NH-W as reference. Models were adjusted for demographics, comorbidities, medications, exposure time, and neighborhood socioeconomics. This cohort consisted of 1,544,541 veterans (70% NH-W, 20% NH-B, 6.0% H-W, 1.2% NH-A, and 0.9% NH-AIAN). In adjusted analyses, compared to NH-Ws, REM veterans had lower mortality in SA (NH-A OR 0.30 [95% CI 0.27-0.33]; NH-NHPI OR 0.79 [95% CI 0.74-0.85], insomnia (NH-A OR 0.34 [95% CI 0.31-0.37]; NH-NHPI OR 0.84 [95% CI 0.74-0.86], and COMISA (NH-A OR 0.28 [95% CI 0.23-0.35]; NH-AIAN OR 0.71 [95% CI 0.61-0.83]. These data suggest that REM veterans using VHA sleep care have lower sleep disorder-related all-cause mortality than NH-White veterans, suggesting attenuated racial-ethnic mortality disparities within this equal-access healthcare setting.

papers.title: Evolution of daytime PaCO2 in patients with neuromuscular disorders and OSA using CPAP: a retrospective study.
papers.abstract: Neuromuscular disorders (NMD) are frequently complicated by obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), which may add an obstructive ventilatory load and contribute to CO2 retention. While non-invasive ventilation (NIV) is recommended for established hypoventilation, the impact of continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) on daytime PaCO2 in NMD remains poorly documented. We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study in a tertiary neuromuscular referral center. Consecutive adults with NMD undergoing respiratory assessment were included if they had (i) OSA treated with CPAP and (ii) daytime PaCO2 measurements before and after CPAP initiation. The primary outcome was paired PaCO2 change. Prespecified analyses were performed in patients with baseline PaCO2 ≥42 and ≥ 45 mmHg. Predictors of PaCO2 decrease were explored using logistic regression. One hundred patients were included, median AHI was 36.9/h. At a median follow-up of 13.6 months, PaCO2 decreased from 42.0 [39.0-44.0] to 40.5 [38.3-43.0] mmHg, corresponding to a paired reduction of 1.0 mmHg (95%CI 0.3-2.0; p = 0.01). PaCO2 decreased in 61% of patients, remained unchanged in 9%, and increased in 30%. In patients with baseline PaCO2≥45 mmHg (n = 18), the median PaCO2 reduction was 1.3 mmHg (95%CI 0.25-2.5; p = 0.016) and 8 patients normalized their PaCO2 but 4 experienced a deterioration. Baseline PaCO2 was the only independent predictor of PaCO2 decrease. In NMD patients with OSA, CPAP was associated with a modest but significant reduction in daytime PaCO2. Responses were heterogeneous, supporting careful patient phenotyping and structured reassessment after CPAP initiation to avoid delayed NIV escalation in non-responders.

papers.title: Prevalence and clinical associations of sleep-disordered breathing in multiple sclerosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), including obstructive and central sleep apnoea, may contribute to fatigue, cognitive impairment, and reduced quality of life in people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS). Reported prevalence varies widely, and the influence of MS-specific factors on SDB risk remains unclear. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies reporting objective measures of SDB in adults with MS. Databases were searched up to July 2025. Pooled prevalence and mean apnoea-hypopnoea or respiratory event index (AHI/REI) were estimated using random-effects models. Meta-regression examined associations with demographic and MS-related factors. Case-control studies were pooled to compare SDB odds in PwMS versus controls. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. 29 studies including 1167 PwMS were included. Pooled prevalence of SDB was 30% (95% CI: 21-40%), with a mean AHI of 7.2 events/hour (95% CI: 4.2-10.2), indicating predominantly mild SDB. Meta-regression identified higher body mass index (BMI), longer disease duration, greater disability (EDSS), and a higher proportion of people with progressive MS in the population studied as predictors of elevated AHI. Case-control studies (n = 7) did not show significantly increased odds of SDB in PwMS versus controls; however, case-control participants had relatively low EDSS scores. Heterogeneity was substantial, and certainty of evidence was very low across outcomes. SDB affects a considerable proportion of PwMS, particularly those with more advanced disease or higher BMI. Although most SDB identified was mild and fatigue in MS has multifactorial origins, the potential contribution of SDB to sleep quality and cognitive function supports targeted screening approaches. Further research should evaluate whether MS-adapted assessment strategies improve detection and whether treatment of SDB improves MS-related outcomes.

papers.title: Between patterns and predictions: Interpretable latent EEG representations for clinical insights.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) captures rich brain dynamics, yet in clinical practice this complexity is often reduced to simplified summaries or categorical labels, limiting its interpretability for decision-making. We tested the hypothesis that a pretrained latent embedding framework, the Universal Map of EEG (UM-EEG), can preserve clinically meaningful structure across heterogeneous datasets and provide a generalizable representation of brain states. We applied UM-EEG, without retraining, to three independent cohorts spanning distinct clinical contexts: long-term EEG recordings from cardiac arrest patients (n = 575), subarachnoid hemorrhage (n = 100), and routine clinical EEG recordings containing physiological and pathological patterns (n = 141). EEG segments were projected into a 128-dimensional space anchored by expert-derived reference states, including wakefulness, sleep stages, ictal-interictal continuum activity, and burst suppression. Across datasets, favorable outcome or physiological recordings were consistently located closer to healthy reference states, whereas poor outcome and pathological recordings shifted toward pathological regions of the embedding space. Trajectory-derived geometric and temporal features discriminated outcome in cardiac arrest (ROC-AUC 0.83) and subarachnoid hemorrhage (ROC-AUC 0.76), and distinguished physiological from pathological routine EEGs (ROC-AUC 0.93). In routine EEG, similarity relationships derived from embedding trajectories correlated with those derived from structured clinical reports, indicating that the latent space recapitulates clinically relevant organization. These findings show that a fixed, semantically structured EEG embedding generalizes across etiologies and recording settings, enabling prognostic stratification and contextual interpretation while preserving the relational structure of brain states.

papers.title: Recruitment, Engagement, Experiences, and Self-Reported Changes in a Digital Patient Activation Intervention to Improve Hemodialysis Session Stability: Mixed Methods Study.
papers.abstract: When chronic kidney disease progresses to end-stage kidney disease, many patients receive in-center hemodialysis. Although lifesaving, hemodialysis is associated with intradialytic hypotension. Peer mentoring and patient activation support in hemodialysis have not been well studied. This Dialysafe study combined patient education and peer mentoring to promote health behaviors supporting prevention of intradialytic hypotension. We aimed to describe recruitment, engagement, completion, and attrition; assess participants' health goals and self-reported behavior changes; and evaluate satisfaction and recommendations for improvement. At 10 Dialysafe hemodialysis centers assigned to patient activation, all eligible English-speaking patients were invited. The intervention comprised 5 educational modules and 5 videoconference peer-mentoring sessions. Mixed methods analyses integrated electronic health record and platform data, postintervention surveys, and clinic operations committee notes. An engagement score (range 0-50) summarized intervention use. Descriptive statistics, t tests, chi-square tests, logistic regression, and zero-inflated Poisson regression were used to assess recruitment, completion (all 5 mentoring sessions), and engagement. Qualitative data were inductively coded and integrated through joint displays. Of the 639 eligible patients, 155 (24.3%) were recruited. Recruited patients were younger than nonrecruited patients (mean 57.6, SD 13.8, vs 64.3, SD 14.7 y; P<.001); each additional year was associated with 4% lower odds of recruitment (odds ratio [OR] 0.96, 95% CI 0.94-0.98; P<.001). Recruitment was more likely among college graduates (OR 1.70, 95% CI 1.02-2.83; P=.04) and patients with sleep disorders (OR 2.27, 95% CI 1.06-4.87; P=.03). Attrition was concentrated before mentoring sessions began. Of recruited patients, 72 of 155 (46.5%) met with a peer mentor and 58 of 155 (37.4%) completed all 5 sessions. Completers were 1.9 years younger (56.4, SD 13.8, vs 58.3, SD 13.9 y) and had Charlson Comorbidity Index scores 0.4 points higher (3.4, SD 2.0, vs 3.0, SD 2.3) than noncompleters. The average engagement score was 18.4 of 50 (SD 20.1). Engagement was higher among men (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 1.33, 95% CI 1.22-1.45; P<.001), Black patients (IRR 1.27, 95% CI 1.16-1.39; P<.001), and patients with dialysis vintage <1 year (IRR 1.22, 95% CI 1.05-1.42; P=.01). Higher Charlson Comorbidity Index scores predicted engagement (IRR 1.04, 95% CI 1.01-1.07; P=.002) and completion (OR 1.37, 95% CI 1.05-1.79; P=.02). Of 79 patients who set goals, 64 (81%) selected communication with the care team; 22 of 54 (40.7%) survey respondents identified this as their main behavior change. Both mentees and mentors identified peer-mentoring sessions as the most valuable component. Among mentee respondents, 55 of 55 (100%) respondents rated the program good or excellent, and 53 of 54 (98.1%) respondents would recommend it. Participants constituted a self-selecting group. Patient-clinician communication was a priority, and participants valued peer mentoring. Digital patient activation intervention strategies to increase reach are needed. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03171545; https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT03171545. RR2-10.2196/46187.

papers.title: [Standardization of quality criteria for continuous glucose monitoring systems in Argentina].
papers.abstract: Although glycated hemoglobin is the standard method for assessing glycemic control in people with diabetes mellitus (DM), this biomarker does not reflect circadian or daily glycemic variations, which means that episodes of hypoglycemia and/or hyperglycemia -which are associated with acute or chronic microvascular and macrovascular complications of DM- may go unnoticed. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) systems provide real-time glucose readings, allowing for the identification of trends and fluctuations throughout the day. These devices facilitate treatment decisions to optimize glucose control. Nevertheless, although CGM devices are associated with clinical benefits, limitations are recognized regarding the need for standardization, reliability, and outcomes across diverse populations and clinical settings. Our objective was to adapt the Consensus on Standardization of CGM Parameters for Latin America to Argentina using the ADAPTE method. Eleven of the existing recommendations were adopted with the addition of best practice guidelines; one recommendation was adapted to optimize its applicability; and three additional recommendations were generated based on expert opinion. The recommendations are directed at all members of the healthcare team who care for people with DM, decision-makers and health policy makers, and healthcare system funders, among others.

papers.title: Outcome selection and reporting transparency in ClinicalTrials.gov-registered chronic spontaneous urticaria trials: a registry-publication linkage study.
papers.abstract: Chronic spontaneous urticaria/chronic idiopathic urticaria (CSU/CIU) trials increasingly evaluate biologics and targeted mast-cell therapies. Whether ClinicalTrials.gov-registered trials consistently capture patient-centred outcomes and disseminate results in a timely and linkable manner remains uncertain. To map registered outcome domains, patient-centred outcome breadth and reporting transparency among interventional CSU/CIU trials in ClinicalTrials.gov. ClinicalTrials.gov was searched using three CSU/CIU-related queries, yielding 486 records and 168 unique NCT registrations after deduplication. Eligible interventional trials were coded for intervention category, trial purpose and nine registered outcome domains. A descriptive 0-8 patient-centred outcome score excluded safety. A stratified sample was independently recoded by a second author. Completed or terminated trials underwent manual registry-publication linkage, with primary and secondary publications distinguished and reporting assessed at 12, 24 and 36 months after primary completion using a fixed data lock of 1 June 2026. We included 128 eligible trials; 83 were completed or terminated. Disease activity/UAS7 (78.1%), itch/pruritus (65.6%) and wheals/hives (59.4%) were commonly registered, whereas urticaria control/UCT (28.1%), angioedema (30.5%), relapse/remission/rescue medication (24.2%) and explicit sleep/daily activity (7.8%) were less frequent. The mean patient-centred score was 3.37 (SD 1.98), and 20 trials (15.6%) scored at least 6. Independent second coding showed 90.4% agreement across 270 domain-level decisions. Among 83 completed/terminated trials, 32 (38.6%) had both posted results and a confirmed primary publication, whereas 15 (18.1%) had no qualifying public result identified. Any qualifying public result was available within 12, 24 and 36 months for 18.8%, 53.5% and 66.7% of trials with sufficient follow-up, respectively. ClinicalTrials.gov-registered CSU/CIU trials show substantial heterogeneity in patient-centred outcome coverage. Distinguishing trial purpose, primary from secondary publications and reporting opportunity over time provides a more cautious assessment of the registered evidence base and highlights opportunities for more harmonised outcome selection and clearer result dissemination.

papers.title: NLGN3 autism variants have distinct functional impact on synapses and sleep behavior in Drosophila.
papers.abstract: Neuroligin-3 (NLGN3) was first identified as a X-linked risk gene associated with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Most reported variants are identified in males who inherited their variants from an unaffected mother, but de novo variants have also been identified in both affected heterozygous females and hemizygous males. The p.R451C variant was the initial variant associating NLGN3 with ASD and has been heavily investigated, yet little is known about the functional consequences of other NLGN3 variants. To determine the functional consequences of other NLGN3 variants in vivo, we generated transgenic Drosophila models corresponding to a de novo variant (p.R175W) identified in a heterozygous female proband with ASD, a maternally inherited variant (p.R451C) identified in a hemizygous male with ASD, and another maternally inherited variant identified in a male (p.R597W) associated with sleep disorder and ASD. In Drosophila, loss of the fly homolog, Nlg3, altered sleep patterns, synaptic architecture, and vesicle dynamics, which were rescued by the expression of the human NLGN3Ref allele. When comparing the variants, the p.R175W variant and the maternally inherited p.R451C variant altered synapse morphology with minimal effects on vesicle dynamics, and the p.R597W variant altered sleep and vesicle dynamics with minimal impact on synapse morphology. Using overexpression models, human NLGN3Ref altered sleep patterns and synaptic morphology. Moreover, the p.R175W variant exacerbated sleep phenotypes, and the p.R175W and p.R451C variants exacerbated synapse morphology phenotypes. Together, our findings suggest that the de novo NLGN3 p.R175W variant identified in a heterozygous female exhibits gain-of-function properties, while maternally inherited variants have context-dependent functional impact. Moreover, some NLGN3 variants disrupt synaptic development, while other variants alter synaptic function, suggesting that NLGN3 variants have differential effects. These functional differences may provide insight into the heterogeneity of individuals with ASD.

papers.title: Reliability and validity of the Japanese version of the Sleep Problem Acceptance Questionnaire.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to develop a Japanese version of the Sleep Problem Acceptance Questionnaire (SPAQ-J) and assess its reliability and validity. The SPAQ-J was developed through a forward-backward translation procedure with permission from the original authors. The sample included 861 adults with insomnia who completed questionnaires on experiential avoidance, insomnia symptoms, dysfunctional beliefs about sleep, sleep-related safety behaviors, insomnia catastrophizing, and pre-sleep arousal. Confirmatory factor analysis confirmed that the SPAQ-J retained the two-factor structure of the original version (CFI = 0.972, TLI = 0.958, RMSEA = 0.082, SRMR = 0.059): Activity Engagement and Willingness. Although internal consistency was adequate (Activity Engagement: α = 0.868, ω = 0.870; Willingness: α = 0.895, ω = 0.895), test-retest reliability was below the recommended threshold (Activity Engagement: ICC = 0.586, Willingness: ICC = 0.589). In terms of construct validity, Willingness moderately correlated with all scales, whereas Activity Engagement showed moderate-to-weak correlations. Hierarchical multiple regression analysis revealed that adding the SPAQ-J subscales significantly enhanced the explanatory power. Measurement invariance analysis across sex and age groups showed no significant changes in the fit indices, indicating stability. These findings suggest that the SPAQ-J is a valid and partially reliable measure of psychological flexibility related to sleep problems in the Japanese population.

papers.title: Concave sparsity-assisted time-reassigned multisynchrosqueezing transform for early-stage weak fault feature enhancement with applications to bearing fault diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Early-stage defects in wind turbine bearings often generate weak impulsive signatures that are easily obscured by strong background noise, posing a significant challenge to accurate extraction of fault-related features. To overcome this limitation, a novel concave sparsity-assisted time-reassigned multisynchrosqueezing transform (CSA-TMSST) is developed to improve the extraction of weak fault-related signatures. First, a non-convex sparse optimization model incorporating the generalized minimax-concave (GMC) penalty is established to reconstruct fault impulsive components from the raw signal. The introduced GMC-based sparse regularization enhances signal sparsity, enabling the accurate extraction of impulsive fault signatures. Subsequently, TMSST is employed to characterize the reconstructed signal in the time-frequency (TF) domain, yielding a more concentrated time-frequency representation (TFR). Furthermore, the iterative reassignment mechanism is utilized to enhance the concentration of TF energy distribution, thereby yielding a clearer TFR of transient fault features. Finally, characteristic fault frequencies are identified via spectral analysis. The results demonstrate that CSA-TMSST is capable of extracting weak fault-related signatures and producing high-quality TFRs under strong noise conditions, confirming its effectiveness and superiority.

papers.title: Concurrent TMS-EEG to characterise interhemispheric signal propagation over the motor and prefrontal regions: An independent replication of GABAB receptor mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Callosal abnormalities disrupt interhemispheric communications that impair the recovery of a series of neurological and psychiatric disorders. Understanding interhemispheric communication could help identify treatments for disorders with dysfunctional callosal transmission. This study aimed to validate the sensitivity of a TMS-EEG-based measure of interhemispheric signal propagation (ISP) to GABAB receptor modulation, while independently replicating the pharmacological mechanisms of interhemispheric inhibition. A group of 29 participants received an oral dose of either baclofen, a GABAB receptor agonist, or a placebo. Before and after drug intake, single-pulse TMS-EEG was applied to assess ISP in both the motor and prefrontal regions. Our findings indicated that baclofen increased interhemispheric inhibition over the motor region, indexed by significantly decreased ISP (p = 0.037). No significant effect was observed in the dorsolateral prefrontal region (p = 0.186), suggesting regional specificity in GABAB receptor modulation of ISP. These findings uncovered the pharmacological mechanisms of interhemispheric inhibition as indexed by ISP. They also highlight the potential of ISP for characterising interhemispheric communication, which could inform the treatment for a series of disorders with dysfunctional callosal transmission.

papers.title: Divergent interplay between STIM1 and STIM2 sets the efficacy of central synapses.
papers.abstract: Stromal interaction molecules (STIMs) are endoplasmic reticulum resident calcium (Ca2+ sensors that modulate Ca2+ homeostasis. Mammals express two isoforms, STIM1 and STIM2, but whether they serve redundant or distinct roles in neurotransmission remains poorly defined. Using Ca2+ imaging and electrophysiology in hippocampal neurons lacking STIM1, STIM2, or both, we examined presynaptic and postsynaptic functions of STIMs at excitatory and inhibitory synapses. Both isoforms redundantly activated store-operated Ca2+ entry and amplified presynaptic Ca2+ influx, sustaining neurotransmitter release by expanding the readily releasable pool of synaptic vesicles and accelerating vesicle replenishment. These presynaptic roles were synapse specific: STIM1 predominantly supported excitatory synapses, whereas STIM2 was critical for the inhibitory counterparts. Postsynaptically, STIM1 and STIM2 exerted opposing effects on glutamate and GABA receptor levels, such that simultaneous loss of both isoforms rescued postsynaptic function. Together, the findings show that STIM1 and STIM2 differentially tune synaptic efficacy according to synapse type and subcellular compartment.

papers.title: Sensitization-related pain phenotypes and their clinical correlates in women with lipedema: A case-control study.
papers.abstract: ObjectivesLipedema is a chronic adipose tissue disorder characterized by disproportionate fat accumulation, lower extremity pain, functional impairment, and reduced quality of life. Although pain is a cardinal symptom, its underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize sensitization-related pain phenotypes in women with lipedema by examining central sensitization (CS) and neuropathic -like pain features and their associations with lower extremity function, sleep quality, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL).MethodsIn this cross-sectional case-control study, 54 women with clinically diagnosed lipedema and 48 age-matched control participants were enrolled between March and October 2025. Pain phenotypes were assessed using the Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI) and Pain-DETECT questionnaire. Lower extremity function, sleep quality, and HRQoL were evaluated using Lower Extremity Functional Scale (LEFS), Jenkins Sleep Scale (JSS), and EuroQol-5D-3L (EQ-5D-3L), respectively.ResultsWomen with lipedema had significantly higher Pain-DETECT and CSI scores than controls, indicating greater neuropathic-like pain features and CS-related symptom burden (both p < .01). They also demonstrated poorer lower extremity function, greater sleep disturbance, and lower HRQoL. Pain-DETECT scores were positively correlated with CSI, anxiety, depression, and sleep disturbance scores. In multivariable analyses, LEFS independently predicted Pain-DETECT scores (B = -0.171, p = .015), whereas anxiety independently predicted CSI scores (B = 1.980, p = .002).ConclusionsWomen with lipedema exhibit prominent sensitization-related pain phenotypes associated with functional impairment, sleep disturbances, and reduced quality of life. Identification of these pain characteristics may improve clinical assessment, patient stratification, and multidisciplinary management of lower extremity symptoms in lipedema.

papers.title: Comment on "Association of peripheral NLRP3 inflammasome activation with prevalent and incident chronic kidney disease in patients with obstructive sleep apnea: a prospective study".
papers.abstract: This correspondence comments on the study by Cai et al. examining circulating NLRP3 and prevalent and incident chronic kidney disease (CKD) in patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). The inclusion of 648 participants, complementary cross-sectional and prospective analyses, and evaluation of estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and albuminuria are important strengths. Nevertheless, several methodological considerations affect interpretation. Prevalent CKD appears to have been classified using baseline eGFR or urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio without consistent confirmation of chronicity. A single baseline NLRP3 measurement may not reflect long-term biological activity, while adjusted associations do not establish improved prediction beyond established risk factors. The possible causal roles of OSA severity, nocturnal hypoxemia, and inflammatory markers also merit explicit consideration. Building on these findings, future multicenter studies should confirm CKD with repeat renal measurements, assess serial NLRP3 reproducibility, prespecify causally informed models, and compare clinical prediction models with and without NLRP3 using discrimination, calibration, validation, and decision-curve analysis. These steps would help determine whether circulating NLRP3 offers meaningful incremental value for renal risk stratification in OSA.

papers.title: The Closer, the Better: Engineering RGB Thermometric Performance in Tb3+,Eu3+-Doped MOFs.
papers.abstract: The effectiveness of luminescence thermometry, which exploits temperature-induced changes in the spectroscopic properties of phosphor materials for temperature sensing, has been extensively demonstrated. However, from a practical perspective, monitoring temperature-induced variations in the color of the emitted light offers a considerably more straightforward and user-friendly alternative to conventional spectral analysis. In this context, establishing a clear relationship between the thermal evolution of the emission color and the structure of the phosphor is essential for the rational design of visual luminescence thermometers. In this work, we investigate the correlation between the temperature-dependent emission color and the structural characteristics of Tb3+,Eu3+-co-doped metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), with particular emphasis on their potential for filter-free, camera-based thermal sensing. The obtained results demonstrate that, within the investigated series of materials, decreasing the interionic distance between Eu3+ and Tb3+ ions increases the probability of energy transfer and consequently enhances the thermal sensitivity of the camera-based readout derived from the ratio of luminescence intensities recorded in the blue and red channels. These findings establish a direct relationship between the structural characteristics of the luminescent material, the underlying energy-transfer processes, and its thermometric performance. More broadly, this study provides a foundation for the rational design of visual luminescence thermometers with predefined sensing characteristics, opening a pathway toward structure-guided optimization of filter-free, camera-based thermal sensing platforms.

papers.title: A Systematic Review of Screen Time and Obesity in Children, Adolescents, and Young Adults: Sex-Specific Pathways and Implications for Public Health Interventions.
papers.abstract: Screen time is associated with multiple adverse health outcomes, including obesity. However, evidence for children and adolescents is limited and inconsistent, and potential sex-specific differences have not been characterized. This systematic review aimed to synthesize evidence on the association between screen time and obesity-related outcomes among children, adolescents, and young adults, with a focus on sex-specific pathways and implications for public health interventions. This systematic review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines and was based on an a priori protocol. Two reviewers independently selected studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Data were synthesized based on the direction of associations and patterns of sex differences. Of the 22 studies included, 18 reported a significant positive association between screen time and obesity-related outcomes. Sex-specific patterns were also observed, with some studies reporting associations only among females (n = 6) or males (n = 4). Among females, observed associations more frequently involved adiposity, metabolically unhealthy obesity, and psychologic factors such as body image concerns and weight dissatisfaction, whereas among males, associations were more often linked to behavioral factors such as increased caloric intake, late-night screen use, and reduced sleep. Our findings indicate that screen time is associated with obesity among children, adolescents, and young adults, with evidence suggesting potential sex differences in the behavioral, physiologic, and psychologic mechanisms. These findings highlight the need for interventions that move beyond simple screen time reduction and consider the mechanisms that may underlie sex-related differences in obesity risk. Potential strategies may include promoting physical activity among girls and addressing problematic screen use, screen-related eating, and sleep disruption among boys, as well as integrating screen-related psychosocial factors into obesity prevention and management. Given the limited number of studies formally assessing sex-screen time interactions, further research is needed to better characterize these observed patterns.

papers.title: Pharmacogenetics in HIV therapy: a review of key biomarkers, regulatory annotations, and clinical dosing guidelines.
papers.abstract: Pharmacogenetics is pivotal in modern HIV management, facilitating the transition from the traditional "one-size-fits-all" model toward personalized precision medicine. By analyzing how unique genetic profiles influence pharmacological responses, clinicians can maximize therapeutic efficacy while minimizing toxicities and adverse drug reactions. Given the high interindividual variability in antiretroviral drug exposure and the necessity for lifelong treatment, identifying key genetic biomarkers is essential to optimize patient safety, treatment adherence, and overall quality of life. This narrative review evaluates major gene-drug associations in HIV therapy, focusing on HLA-B * 57:01 for abacavir, UGT1A1 for atazanavir and dolutegravir, and CYP2B6 for efavirenz. The research includes an exhaustive review of pharmacogenomic databases (e.g. ClinPGx), regulatory agency labels (FDA, EMA, Swissmedic, HC-SC, PMDA), and clinical guidelines from CPIC and DPWG. Integrating pharmacogenetics into clinical practice significantly improves patient safety and treatment adherence. While HLA-B * 57:01 screening is widely implemented, barriers remain for other markers, including logistical challenges and the lack of genomic representation for African and Latin American populations. Clinicians must utilize evidence-based resources and remain updated on this evolving field to effectively tailor antiretroviral regimens and practice precision medicine.

papers.title: Losing Sleep, Gaining Weight? Young Bangladeshi Adults' Perceptions of Sleep, Eating and Body Weight: A Qualitative Study.
papers.abstract: Inadequate sleep and excess body weight are escalating global health concerns, especially among young adults facing academic pressures, digital lifestyles, and cultural norms. While quantitative research has shown links between sleep and body weight, little is known about the lived experiences shaping this relationship in Asian contexts. A qualitative study was conducted in urban Dhaka, Bangladesh, in 2022. Twenty-six young adults aged 18-25 years were recruited through purposive and snowball sampling methods. Semi-structured, in-depth interviews were conducted in Bangla, audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and translated into English. Thematic analysis was performed using an inductive approach, supplemented by deductive coding based on the socio-ecological model (SEM). Five key themes emerged: (1) structural and environmental conditions disrupting sleep; (2) digital night culture and socially reinforced wakefulness; (3) the prioritisation of productivity over sleep; (4) unequal burdens of household labour and caregiving and opportunities for rest; and (5) perceived associations between irregular sleep, fatigue, and eating behaviours. Young adults described poor sleep as both a personal and structural issue and perceived connections with body weight and overall wellbeing. Across the identified themes, sleep and eating practices that appeared individual were embedded within interpersonal, institutional, environmental, and sociocultural contexts. The findings indicate opportunities for healthy sleep are influenced by social, institutional, and environmental conditions in addition to individual practices. Consequently, sleep-health strategies targeting young adults may benefit from integrating individual education with interventions that address peer and family practices, institutional expectations, and environments conducive to sleep health. Further longitudinal and mixed-method research is required to investigate the pathways identified in these qualitative accounts. The findings were discussed with patient and public involvement (PPI) members who are young adults. Their insights informed the development of the interview guide. A subset of participants helped interpret the results by engaging in member checking of preliminary findings and identified themes. Members of the public did not participate in study governance or manuscript preparation.
papers.journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy

papers.title: Successful Guidewire-Guided Ethanol Ablation for PVCs Originating From Epicardial Anterior Interventricular Groove Adjacent to LAD.
papers.abstract: Premature ventricular complexes (PVCs) originating from epicardial anterior interventricular groove and closely adjacent to the left anterior descending artery (LAD) are difficult to eliminate and carry high risks of coronary damage or occlusion. We describe a successful guidewire-assisted ethanol ablation in this high -risk patient. A 30-year-old man who presented with palpitations and high-burden PVCs was admitted to our hospital. Pace mapping performed at the epicardial anterior interventricular groove yielded QRS morphology nearly identical to the native PVCs. Coronary angiography revealed that the target site was directly adjacent to the proximal-middle segment of the LAD. Guidewire-assisted ethanol ablation via a small branch of the anterior interventricular vein successfully eliminated the PVCs. Postprocedural coronary angiography showed no coronary artery injury and the patient remained free of PVCs during the 2-month follow-up period. Epicardial PVCs arising within the anterior interventricular groove where the LAD runs carry a high risk of coronary artery injury during ablation. Guidewire-assisted anhydrous ethanol ablation serves as an effective and safe therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Tachycardia Initiation by Dual-Mode PVC on Ambulatory ECG: Pattern Discovery and Invasive Electrophysiological Characteristics.
papers.abstract: Mechanisms of premature ventricular complex (PVC)-induced long-RP tachycardia warrant investigation. A 57-year-old man with palpitations underwent 24-hour ambulatory electrocardiogram (ECG). The recording showed 4,150 monomorphic PVCs and 800 episodes of long-RP tachycardia, all triggered by the same PVC morphology. Two initiation patterns emerged. One involved direct retrograde conduction, the other showed retrograde conduction only after PR prolongation. In both patterns, induction occurred across a broad range of PVC coupling intervals. Invasive electrophysiology study (EPS) then demonstrated slow-slow atrioventricular nodal re-entrant tachycardia (SS-AVNRT) involving multiple atrioventricular nodal pathways, consistent with the dual-mode patterns seen on ambulatory ECG. Ablation succeeded, with no recurrence at 6 months. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of SS-AVNRT to show distinctive PVC-induced tachycardia patterns on ambulatory ECG, corroborated by EPS. Ambulatory ECG patterns of PVC-triggered long-RP tachycardia may suggest a dual-pathway substrate for SS-AVNRT, warranting EPS confirmation.

papers.title: Novel SCN5A Variant in a Patient With Dilated Cardiomyopathy Complicated by Conduction Disorders and Recurrent Ventricular Arrhythmias.
papers.abstract: Although sodium voltage-gated channel alpha subunit 5 (SCN5A) was traditionally linked to electrophysiological disorders, growing evidence underscores its significant involvement in structural abnormalities. A young dilated cardiomyopathy patient presented with a distinctive electro-structural dual phenotype, characterized by progressive left ventricular systolic dysfunction, conduction disorders, and concomitant severe ventricular arrhythmias. Comorbidities included coronary artery disease, chronic kidney disease, obesity, and obstructive sleep apnea. Genetic testing identified a de novo heterozygous nonsense variant in the SCN5A gene. Comprehensive management included guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure, antiarrhythmic agents, along with comorbidities management and risk factor modification. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of dilated cardiomyopathy in young patients with multiple overlapping etiologies-genetic, ischemic, metabolic. A de novo SCN5A variant may contribute to the arrhythmic phenotype and progressive cardiomyopathy. Beyond its classical electrophysiological role, SCN5A is increasingly implicated in structural remodeling. This case emphasizes the complexity of genotype-phenotype correlation and gene-environment interaction.

papers.title: Exercise-Induced Ventricular Arrhythmia: Initial Presentation of Occult Barlow Syndrome Unmasked by Stress Testing.
papers.abstract: Barlow syndrome, a form of myxomatous mitral valve prolapse, often presents with nonspecific symptoms and may be missed on resting examination. A 38-year-old woman presented with recurrent palpitations triggered by stress and poor sleep. Resting physical examination was unremarkable. Exercise stress test (EST) revealed frequent premature ventricular contractions and a midlate systolic apical click postexercise, which were both previously absent at rest. Echocardiography confirmed Barlow syndrome with 7 mm mitral annular disjunction (MAD). Beta-blocker therapy was initiated with symptomatic improvement. The EST unmasked both electrophysiological and auscultatory abnormalities entirely occult on standard resting evaluation. This case offers a practical diagnostic reference for recognizing latent cardiac diseases in patients with nonspecific symptoms. EST plays a crucial role in diagnosing atypical Barlow syndrome by unmasking both arrhythmias and characteristic auscultatory findings. Beta-blocker therapy effectively improves symptoms in patients with mitral annular disjunction-associated exercise-induced arrhythmias.

papers.title: Caregiver and Family Factors Related to Life's Essential 8 in Young Children.
papers.abstract: Promotion of cardiovascular health (CVH) during young childhood is critical for preventing later disease. This study describes the CVH of 269 young children from an observational cohort study and examines child, caregiver, and family factors related to CVH. Child anthropometrics were measured. Parents reported on child smoking exposure, sleep, physical activity, diet, and possible CVH correlates. CVH composite scores were calculated using the American Heart Association Life's Essential 8 (LE8) framework. The average LE8 score for the sample was in the moderate CVH range (74.8 ± 10.2). Most children had no smoking exposure (92%), met sleep recommendations (66%), and had a healthy weight (76%). Few children met recommendations for physical activity or diet. Caregiver (education, age, health) and family (household size, insurance) factors related to CVH. CVH promotion efforts for young children should target physical activity, diet, and caregiver and family factors.
papers.journal: Journal of pediatric health care : official publication of National Association of Pediatric Nurse Associates & Practitioners

papers.title: Depression and anxiety among older surgical patients with cognitive impairment: a multicenter longitudinal cohort study.
papers.abstract: Cognitive impairment (CI), depression, and anxiety are underrecognized yet frequently co-existing conditions linked to poor surgical outcomes in older patients. We examined: 1) the prevalence and perioperative trajectory of depression/anxiety in patients with and without CI; 2) preoperative patient-reported outcome measures; and 3) postoperative outcomes associated with depression/anxiety. This study included 369 surgical patients (≥65 years) from two academic tertiary care hospitals. CI was assessed with the Ascertain Dementia Eight preoperatively, while depression/anxiety was measured using the Patient Health Questionnaire-4 preoperatively, at 30-, and 90 days postoperatively. The trajectory of depression/anxiety in CI versus no-CI patients was analyzed with linear mixed-effects models. Preoperatively, 28% of patients had depression/anxiety, 13% had CI, and 8% had co-existing depression/anxiety and CI. Those with depression/anxiety were more likely to have co-existing CI than those without depression/anxiety (29% vs. 6%; P<0.001). Patients that screened positive for preoperative CI experienced significantly worse psychological symptoms at all times compared to those without CI. Among those with preoperative CI, mean psychological symptoms remained above screening thresholds for depression/anxiety at all time points and significantly worsened at 90 days post-surgery compared to baseline levels. Patients with depression/anxiety reported significantly worse preoperative health, including greater pain and functional disability, as well as worse quality of life and sleep. Given greater psychological burden in those with CI, screening for both conditions may enable early identification of patients at higher risk for poor outcomes. This approach may ultimately enhance risk stratification and optimization of perioperative care in older adults.

papers.title: Video EEG in pediatric epilepsy: Diagnostic significance and association between frequency band power and cognitive impairment severity.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to compare video electroencephalogram (VEEG) and routine electroencephalogram (EEG) in childhood epilepsy diagnosis and analyze the correlation between EEG frequency band power and cognitive impairment severity. One hundred and sixty children suspected of having epilepsy underwent routine EEG and VEEG examinations. Diagnostic efficacy and detection rates were compared. Cognitive function was evaluated in 80 children diagnosed with epilepsy, who were allocated into normal intelligence (35 cases), borderline intelligence (25 cases), and intelligence-impaired (20 cases) groups. Clinical data, EEG parameters, and their correlation with cognitive impairment were analyzed. VEEG showed higher sensitivity, accuracy, and negative predictive value, and detection rates of epileptiform discharges, synchronous clinical seizures, and clinical symptoms than routine EEG (p < 0.05). Clinical characteristics and EEG parameters differed among the three groups (p < 0.05). The relative power of δ and θ bands and the awake and sleep discharge indices were positively correlated with cognitive impairment severity (r = 0.300, 0.643, 0.622, and 0.456), whereas α and β band power were negatively correlated (r = -0.515 and -0.410) (all p < 0.001). VEEG demonstrated higher diagnostic performance than routine EEG, and EEG frequency band power was correlated with cognitive impairment severity.

papers.title: Association between low-carbohydrate diet scores and macrovascular events or all-cause mortality in adults with type 1 diabetes in Japan.
papers.abstract: The effects of lifestyle factors on macrovascular events or all-cause mortality remain unclear in type 1 diabetes. We examined the associations of diet, physical activity, and sleep with these outcomes among adults with type 1 diabetes living in Japan. This multicenter prospective cohort included 352 adults with type 1 diabetes from the Juntendo-Aso Type 1 Diabetes cohort. Lifestyle factors were assessed by questionnaire. Dietary intake was evaluated using a brief-type self-administered diet history questionnaire, from which Total, Plant, and Animal low-carbohydrate diet scores were calculated. The primary composite outcome was the first occurrence of ischemic heart disease, cerebrovascular disease, peripheral artery disease, or all-cause mortality. Associations were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models. Mean age was 51.4 ± 15.1 years, mean HbA1c was 7.9 ± 1.1%, and carbohydrate accounted for 49.3% of energy intake. During follow-up, 35 participants experienced the primary composite outcome. In multivariable Cox models, the Total LCDS (HR, 0.90; 95% CI: 0.82-0.98; P = 0.012), Plant LCDS (HR, 0.85; 95% CI: 0.76-0.94; P = 0.003), and Animal LCDS (HR, 0.93; 95% CI: 0.87-0.996; P = 0.037) were inversely associated with the outcome. Among adults with type 1 diabetes living in Japan, low-carbohydrate dietary patterns, particularly the Plant low-carbohydrate diet score, were inversely associated with macrovascular events or all-cause mortality.

papers.title: Reversal of refractory epilepsy in an adult with GAMT deficiency: A case report and comparative literature review.
papers.abstract: Guanidinoacetate methyltransferase (GAMT) deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive creatine biosynthesis disorder. Reports specifically focusing on adult patients remain scarce. We report a 52-year-old female (the oldest documented case of GAMT deficiency to date) presenting with severe intellectual disability, refractory epilepsy, and adult-onset disease progression. Whole-exome sequencing identified novel compound heterozygous GAMT variants (c.265_267del and c.253G>T), and magnetic resonance spectroscopy confirmed cerebral creatine depletion. Remarkably, initiating oral creatine supplementation at age 52 achieved complete seizure freedom, normalization of the electroencephalogram (EEG), and significant motor function recovery. A comprehensive review revealed that untreated adult patients face a high risk of progressive neurological deterioration. Compared to the pediatric cohort, adults exhibited a significantly higher prevalence of movement disorders (69.2% vs. 33.1%, p < 0.001) and a trend toward a higher prevalence of epilepsy (92.3% vs. 74.2%). Especially, atonic seizures (drop attacks) are particularly characteristic of adult GAMT deficiency, with EEGs frequently demonstrating background slowing, multifocal epileptiform discharges, and electrodecremental patterns. This study underscores that continuous disease progression and prolonged neurotoxicity still could compromise the well-being of adult GAMT deficiency patients. Accurate diagnosis is essential for adults presenting with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) phenotype, as even late treatment for GAMT deficiency can still dramatically alleviate the epileptic burden and reverse motor decline. We report the oldest known adult diagnosed with GAMT deficiency. Our case demonstrates that starting creatine treatment even at age 52 can dramatically reduce seizures and restore motor function. Literature shows that untreated adults suffer from more severe epilepsy and movement disorders than children, with symptoms worsening over time. These findings highlight the critical need for genetic testing in adults with unexplained severe epilepsy; timely creatine supplementation can halt cognitive decline and significantly restore quality of life.

papers.title: Frequent involvement of cingulate and insulo-opercular regions in sleep-related hypermotor epilepsy: A multimodal presurgical study.
papers.abstract: Sleep-related hypermotor epilepsy (SHE) is classically considered a frontal lobe epilepsy; however, accumulating evidence suggests that hypermotor seizures may arise from multiple frontal and extrafrontal regions. We characterized the anatomical distribution of best available localizations in patients with SHE using multimodal presurgical data. We retrospectively analyzed 17 patients with clinically diagnosed SHE who underwent comprehensive evaluation, including long-term video-electroencephalographic (EEG) monitoring, 3-T high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography, and, where indicated, magnetoencephalography, stereo-EEG (SEEG), and surgical assessment. Best available anatomical localizations were assigned using a hierarchical multimodal framework incorporating surgical, SEEG, and concordant noninvasive findings. Their anatomical distribution was subsequently assessed at the cohort level. Sixteen patients (94.1%) had an assigned best available localization. Cingulate or insulo-opercular regions were involved in 11 of 16 patients (68.8%), whereas the remaining cases were localized to other frontal regions. In a sensitivity analysis restricted to 10 patients with SEEG-defined and/or surgically supported localizations, six involved cingulate or insulo-opercular regions. All patients were MRI-negative. In contrast, MRI-positron emission tomography fusion provided regionally informative anatomical findings in 16 of 17 cases and contributed to multimodal localization. Interictal epileptiform discharges were identified in 15 patients, whereas regionally informative ictal scalp EEG patterns were observed in eight; ictal interpretation was frequently limited by rapid propagation, movement-related artifacts, and delayed EEG onset. Focal cortical dysplasia-related histopathological findings were identified in five of seven resected specimens, whereas interpretation in two was limited by prior thermocoagulation. These descriptive findings indicate that cingulate and insulo-opercular regions were frequently represented among the identified localizations in this presurgical cohort. Multimodal evaluation integrating electroclinical, imaging, and invasive findings may support presurgical localization in MRI-negative SHE.

papers.title: American Heart Association Life's Essential 8 and Heart Failure in Black Individuals: An Analysis of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
papers.abstract: Self-reported Black individuals have a disproportionately high prevalence of heart failure (HF) compared with other racial groups. In an effort to empower patients and health providers to combat cardiovascular disease, the American Heart Association identified Life's Essential 8 as the 8 health behaviors crucial for heart health. In this study, we evaluate the association between components of Life's Essential 8 and HF outcomes among Black individuals. This cross-sectional observational study analyzed 107 622 individuals captured in the NHANES (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey) from 1999 to 2020 who were categorized by self-reported race. To represent Life's Essential 8, variables of self-reported sleep duration, physical activity, smoking status, and dietary habits were used. Additionally, self-reported diagnoses of diabetes, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, and heart failure were included. Multivariable logistic regression models were constructed to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% CIs for the associations between Life's Essential 8 components and HF among Black individuals. Black individuals were diagnosed with HF at a younger age compared with White individuals (54 years vs 65 years, P<0.001). Among Black individuals, body mass index (odds ratio [OR], 1.041 [95% CI, 1.027-1.055], P=0.02), hypertension (OR, 3.175 [95% CI, 2.14-4.69], P<0.0001), hyperlipidemia (OR, 1.36 [95% CI, 1.04-1.76], P=0.02), and diabetes (OR, 2.07 [95% CI, 1.60-2.67], P≤0.0001) were associated with increased odds of HF. Physical activity was associated with lower odds (OR, 0.564 [95% CI, 0.38-0.836], P=0.004) of HF in Black individuals. Black individuals experienced HF at significantly younger ages, with traditional cardiometabolic factors (body mass index, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes) each independently being associated with HF risk. Physical activity appears protective, underscoring the importance of early, targeted prevention strategies.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

papers.title: Epileptic seizure onset early warning using a lightweight multimodal self-explainable neural network.
papers.abstract: BackgroundCutting-edge deep learning algorithms are applied to epileptic seizures to uncover hidden patterns and achieve high accuracy. Post hoc algorithms explain black-box models but do not reveal the detailed workings of the algorithms. Therefore, intrinsic methods overcome these issues; however, they suffer from improper use of indicative metrics and performance-to-accuracy trade-offs.ObjectiveThis study implements a lightweight multimodal explainable Neural Network for real-time early warning of epileptic seizure onset.MethodsPeople with drug-resistant epilepsy across all age groups who had regular follow-up at Emanuel Mental Specialized Hospital in Ethiopia during the data collection period were the study population. EEG recordings were performed using the 10/20 system. A pretest was conducted two weeks before actual data collection. EDFbrowser was used for preparing the dataset in CSV format. Learned and identity self-explainable neural network algorithms were used to develop a model. In addition to classical evaluation metrics, explicitness, faithfulness, stability, and clear patterns behind predictions were used. Ethical approval was also obtained from the institutional review board (IRB) with reference number No: AM/146/2/36.ResultsLearned and identity self-explainable neural networks were developed and compared. The models' accuracies are 96.524% and 95.328%, and their stability mean values are 99.88% and 99.88%, respectively. Additionally, explicitness values of 0.0055 and 0.01197 were achieved, respectively.ConclusionThe results demonstrate that using a self-explainable neural network is a promising step toward responsible and transparent artificial intelligence. Comparing the two models shows that the learned self-explainable neural network is slightly more optimistic than the identity self-explainable neural network.
papers.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine

papers.title: Factors associated with cytology triage attendance after a hrHPV-positive self-sample and age-related differences: The lifelines cohort.
papers.abstract: BackgroundSelf-sampling for high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing has been introduced in cervical cancer screening programs to improve participation. In the Netherlands, women with an hrHPV-positive self-sample are required to visit their GP's office for cytology triage, as this cannot be performed on self-sampled material. Non-attendance at this step reduces screening effectiveness. This study examined whether sociodemographic and health-related behavioural factors commonly associated with screening participation are also associated with cytology triage attendance after an hrHPV-positive self-sample and whether these associations differ by age.MethodsWe conducted a study on the Lifelines cohort of participants in the Dutch cervical cancer screening program who used self-sampling between 2017 and 2024. The main outcome was cytology triage attendance within 6 months after an hrHPV-positive self-sample. Lifelines contains data on sociodemographic and behavioural factors including education, income, marital status, smoking, alcohol, diet, body mass index, physical activity, television viewing, sleep duration, lifetime use of hormonal contraception, parity, number of children and age at first childbirth. Logistic regression analyses were performed, including age-stratified models.ResultsAmong women with an hrHPV-positive self-sample, 10.2% did not attend cytology triage within 6 months. Most sociodemographic and lifestyle factors were not associated with cytology triage attendance, and no meaningful differences were observed between age groups. However, inadequate prior screening history was associated with lower odds of cytology triage attendance.ConclusionsThe lack of associations with lifestyle or sociodemographic factors suggest that program-level strategies such as how hrHPV test results are communicated, might be more effective in increasing triage participation than interventions targeting specific subgroups.

papers.title: Development of Ester-Based Covalent Organic Framework Film Optical Waveguides for Their Competitive SO2 Gas Sensing Application.
papers.abstract: Ester-based covalent organic frameworks (COFs) demonstrate improved sensing stability and enhanced dipole-dipole (μ-μ) interactions for competitive SO2 sensing upon various acidic gases. An ester-based COF, referred to as [H4bptc-TOPT]n-COF, was synthesized using biphenyl-3,3',5,5'-tetracarboxylic acid (H4bptc) monomer and 4,4',4″-(1,3,5-triazine-2,4,6-triyl) triphenol (TOPT) linker through a one-pot solvothermal method. The resulting COF films were optically transparent and exhibited an irregular hexagonal mesoporous architecture and a high refractive index (from 1.7247 to1.9073), which supports strong single-mode (TE0) guided light, meeting the essential criteria for an optical waveguide sensor (OWGS). As an OWGS, the [H4bptc-TOPT]n-COF film demonstrated high efficiency in SO2 sensing upon various acidic gases. The spectral analysis and density-functional theory computations indicated that the ester group and benzene ring in [H4bptc-TOPT]n-COF contribute to SO2 sensing through μ-μ interactions, which are associated with increased adsorption energy, elongated ester bond length, and reduced bond angles, leading to an increase in the refractive index, adsorption coefficient, and almost reversible morphological change of the [H4bptc-TOPT]n-COF. The presented OWGS features a fast response (tres = 2 s), a wide detection range (100 ppm to 10 ppb), a low detection limit (2.5 ppb), and excellent resistance to interference at 293 K despite its weak immunity to humidity. Furthermore, SO2 adsorption weight of 17.18 ng·cm-2 was determined on per unit area of the [H4bptc-TOPT]n-COF film surface upon μ-μ interactions.

papers.title: Evening chronotype and incidence of all-cause dementia and subtypes after accounting for other sleep traits: A prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: BackgroundChronotype may affect neurophysiology, but whether its association with dementia persists independent of other sleep traits remains uncertain.ObjectiveTo examine associations of chronotype with incident dementia subtypes and potential modification by metabolic and social factors.MethodsIn 443,906 dementia-free participants, Cox models estimated dementia risk after adjustment for sociodemographic, lifestyle, clinical, apolipoprotein E (APOE) genotype, and sleep-related factors. We tested baseline interactions and robustness using multiple imputation, competing-risk models, and landmark analyses.ResultsOver a mean follow-up of 12.5 years, 6355 incident dementia cases were documented. Evening chronotype was associated with a small increased risk of all-cause dementia compared with morning types (HR, 1.07; 95% CI, 1.01-1.14). This association was observed primarily in "other dementias" (HR, 1.12; 1.04-1.21), with no significant association with Alzheimer's disease or vascular dementia (VaD).Exploratory subgroup analyses identified two interactions that remained significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction: social visit frequency for all-cause dementia and napping for VaD (FDR-adjusted p for interaction is 0.024 for both). Evening chronotype was associated with higher all-cause dementia risk among participants reporting infrequent social visits and with higher VaD risk among those reporting usual napping.ConclusionsEvening chronotype was associated with a small increase in the hazard of all-cause dementia after multivariable adjustment. Given the modest magnitude and observational design, evening chronotype may be considered a potential risk marker rather than an independent or causal risk factor. These findings require independent replication.

papers.title: Empagliflozin in Lafora disease: A first-in-human 6-month pilot study with electroclinical and FDG-PET findings.
papers.abstract: Lafora disease (LD) is a rare, fatal neurodegenerative epilepsy with no approved treatments. Empagliflozin, a sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor, has shown neuroprotective actions in preclinical models through modulation of glycogen metabolism, induction of a pseudo-ketogenic state, improved mitochondrial efficiency, and reduction of excitatory neurotransmission. Based on this rationale, we conducted a first-in-human pilot study of empagliflozin in two genetically confirmed LD patients. Two patients with genetically confirmed LD received empagliflozin 10 mg/day for 6 months. Serial assessments included safety and tolerability, seizure frequency, myoclonus severity, electroencephalographic findings, neuropsychological and motor evaluations, brain MRI, and quantitative FDG-PET with regional Z-score analysis. Empagliflozin was safe and well tolerated, with no serious adverse events. Seizure frequency, myoclonus, and overall clinical status remained largely stable over 6 months, although some neuropsychological and motor measures showed variable changes between patients. EEG background activity and spike index were largely unchanged. Brain MRI showed stable mild cortical atrophy in both patients. In contrast, FDG-PET revealed progressive and spatially expanding cerebral hypometabolism in both patients, with worsening regional Z-scores, particularly in the parietal and precuneus regions. In this first-in-human, 6-month pilot study, empagliflozin showed acceptable short-term safety and feasibility in LD, but no definitive conclusions on efficacy can be drawn. The dissociation between relative electroclinical stability and progressive metabolic impairment suggests that quantitative FDG-PET may represent a sensitive biomarker for monitoring disease trajectory in this ultra-rare epilepsy.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape

papers.title: Salivary Dim-Light Melatonin Onset is Associated with Functional Decline, Respiratory Symptom Emergence, and Survival in Early Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis.
papers.abstract: Sleep-wake and circadian disturbances are increasingly recognized in people living with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (plwALS), but endogenous circadian phase timing and its prognostic significance in early disease remain unclear. We assessed whether salivary dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO), an objective marker of central circadian phase, is altered in early plwALS and whether it provides prognostic information. In this prospective longitudinal observational study, plwALS within 18 months of symptom onset underwent home-based salivary melatonin sampling under dim-light conditions at 6 predefined time points around habitual sleep onset. Melatonin profiles were modeled using cubic smoothing splines, and DLMO was defined when the fitted curve first reached 3 pg/ml. Clinical, respiratory, and sleep assessments were collected at baseline (T0) and after 6 months (T6); a subgroup repeated saliva sampling at T6. Age- and sex-matched controls underwent melatonin profiling. Associations with disease progression, incident respiratory symptoms, and survival/tracheostomy were examined using regressions and survival analyses. A total of 50 plwALS were enrolled. Compared with controls, plwALS showed an earlier DLMO (20:24 ± 1:18 vs 20:58 ± 0:50; p = 0.028) despite similar habitual sleep onset and chronotype. Within ALS cohort, a later baseline DLMO correlated with worse functional/motor status, faster progression of disease, incident dyspnea/orthopnea by T6 (adjusted OR 3.11; p = 0.019), and poorer survival/tracheostomy-free outcome. In the resampled subgroup (n = 28), DLMO and melatonin-derived metrics did not change over ~6 months. Circadian phase alterations are detectable in early ALS. Baseline DLMO showed exploratory associations with functional, respiratory, and survival outcomes. Larger independent cohorts are required before DLMO can be considered a validated prognostic biomarker. ANN NEUROL 2026.

papers.title: Pain Severity Trajectories and Patient Profiles in Chronic Pain Patients Treated with Cannabis-Based Medicinal Products: A k-Means Clustering Analysis of the UK Medical Cannabis Registry.
papers.abstract: Cannabis-based medicinal products (CBMPs) are increasingly prescribed for chronic pain, yet the supporting evidence remains limited and the extent to which patients differ in their response is poorly understood. This study applied longitudinal k-means clustering to pain-severity trajectories in patients treated with CBMPs for chronic pain to distinguish patterns of response and identify the baseline characteristics predicting them over 24 months. A cohort study was undertaken of UK Medical Cannabis Registry participants whose primary indication was chronic pain. Pain, health-related quality of life, anxiety, and sleep were assessed with patient-reported outcome measures, including the Brief Pain Inventory Short Form (BPI-SF), EuroQol 5-Dimension 5-Level (EQ-5D-5L), Generalised Anxiety Disorder-7, and Single-Item Sleep Quality Scale, at baseline up to 24 months. BPI-SF pain-severity trajectories were grouped by longitudinal k-means clustering. The number of clusters was chosen using the gap statistic and predictors of cluster membership were examined by logistic regression. Of 3744 patients included, every outcome improved from baseline to 24 months, including BPI-SF pain severity (d = 0.57), pain interference (d = 0.59), and the EQ-5D-5L index value (d = -0.76; all P < .001). More than half of patients achieved a minimal clinically important difference in each pain measure at 24 months. Five distinct trajectory clusters emerged. All ended below their baseline severity, but the magnitude and pattern of change varied markedly. Adverse events were reported by 14.37% (n = 538) of patients, predominantly mild or moderate. Baseline sleep quality, anxiety, and treatment indication were more strongly associated with response than product- or dose-related factors.

papers.title: Dynamic within-person associations between problematic social media use and sleep quality among university students: The mediating role of nomophobia and the moderating role of trait rumination.
papers.abstract: Problematic social media use (PSMU) and poor sleep quality are prevalent among university students. Although previous research has documented associations between PSMU and sleep problems, less is known about the short-term dynamic mechanisms underlying this relationship and the individual differences that may shape vulnerability. Drawing on intensive longitudinal data and dynamic structural equation modeling, this study examined a moderated mediation model in which nomophobia (i.e. anxiety or distress arising from being unable to access or use one's mobile phone) mediated the association between PSMU and poor sleep quality, with trait rumination examined as a moderator of this indirect association. A 21-day daily diary study was conducted with 228 Chinese university students. At the between-person level, higher PSMU was associated with greater nomophobia and poorer sleep quality. At the within-person level, increases in PSMU were prospectively associated with greater nomophobia, which subsequently predicted poorer sleep quality, supporting an indirect association through nomophobia. This indirect association was more pronounced among students with higher levels of trait rumination. By capturing dynamic day-to-day processes, these findings extend current understanding of how PSMU may contribute to poorer sleep during emerging adulthood and highlight nomophobia and rumination as potential targets for interventions aimed at promoting healthier digital habits and sleep.
